Title: HTTP caching - HTTP | MDN
URL: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Caching
Content excerpt:
HTTP caching stores a response associated with a request and reuses the stored response for subsequent requests.

The `Cache-Control` header holds directives for caching in both requests and responses.

Excerpted relevant section:
`no-store`
The `no-store` response directive indicates that any caches of any kind (private or shared) should not store this response.

`no-cache`
The `no-cache` response directive indicates that the response can be stored in caches, but the response must be validated with the origin server before each reuse.

Additional nearby text:
If you don't want the response stored in any cache, use `no-store`.
If you just mean that it should not be reused without validation, use `no-cache`.

Example snippet:
Cache-Control: no-cache
Cache-Control: no-store

Related page discovered in links:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Cache-Control

turns.tool_response:
Title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
URL: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111
Content excerpt:
Section 5.2 Cache-Control

`no-store`
The no-store response directive indicates that a cache MUST NOT store any part of either the immediate request or the response and MUST NOT use the response to satisfy any other request.

`no-cache`
The no-cache response directive, in its unqualified form, indicates that the response MUST NOT be used to satisfy any other request without forwarding it for validation and receiving a successful response.

Nearby clarifying text:
This allows an origin server to prevent a cache from using the response to satisfy a request without contacting it, even by caches that have been configured to return stale responses.

Interpretation:
The RFC language is consistent with MDN's plain-English explanation: `no-store` forbids storage, while `no-cache` allows storage but requires validation before reuse.

Tokio

A runtime for writing reliable, asynchronous, and slim applications with the Rust programming language.

Why Tokio?

Fast

Tokio is built for speed. Its lightweight task model and efficient scheduling enable applications to handle massive amounts of concurrent work. The work-stealing scheduler ensures all CPU cores are utilized effectively.

Reliable

Tokio leverages Rust's ownership, type system, and concurrency model to reduce bugs and ensure thread safety. APIs are designed to be misuse-resistant.

Scalable

Tokio has a minimal footprint and handles backpressure and cancellation naturally. The multi-threaded runtime scales to utilize all available cores while the single-threaded runtime provides a lighter alternative.

Runtime Features

  • Multi-threaded, work-stealing scheduler
  • Cooperative task yielding
  • Timer and timeout support
  • Async TCP/UDP/Unix sockets
  • Async filesystem operations
  • Synchronization primitives

Ecosystem

Tokio provides the foundation for many popular crates including Hyper, Tonic, Axum, and more. The tokio-console tool provides async task debugging.

async-std

Async version of the Rust standard library

async-std is a foundation of portable Rust software, a set of minimal and battle-tested shared abstractions for the broader Rust ecosystem. It offers std types, like Future and Stream, library-defined operations on language primitives, standard macros, I/O and multithreading, among many other things.

Our Philosophy

async-std aims to be a direct async counterpart to the Rust standard library. If you know std, you already know async-std. We believe async Rust should feel as natural as synchronous Rust.

Key Principles

  • Familiar APIs: Mirror std naming and patterns wherever possible
  • Minimal learning curve: If you can use std::fs::read_to_string, you can use async_std::fs::read_to_string
  • Portability: Works on all platforms Rust supports
  • Stability: Careful API design with long-term compatibility in mind

Features

  • Async File I/O
  • Async Networking (TCP, UDP, Unix)
  • Async Process spawning
  • Async synchronization primitives
  • Timer support
  • Task spawning with configurable executors

Performance

async-std uses a sophisticated task scheduler that adapts to workload patterns. While we prioritize API clarity, performance remains excellent for most use cases.

The OWASP API Security Project focuses on strategies and solutions to understand and mitigate the unique vulnerabilities and security risks of APIs.

OWASP API Security Top 10 2023

The OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 is a standard awareness document for developers and web application security.

  1. API1:2023 - Broken Object Level Authorization - APIs expose endpoints that handle object identifiers, creating a wide attack surface.
  2. API2:2023 - Broken Authentication - Authentication mechanisms are often implemented incorrectly.
  3. API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization - Lack of or improper authorization validation at object property level.
  4. API4:2023 - Unrestricted Resource Consumption - APIs do not limit size or number of resources requested.
  5. API5:2023 - Broken Function Level Authorization - Complex access control policies with different hierarchies.
  6. API6:2023 - Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows - Exposing business flows without compensating controls.
  7. API7:2023 - Server Side Request Forgery - SSRF flaws when API fetches remote resources.
  8. API8:2023 - Security Misconfiguration - Misconfigured security settings, unnecessary features enabled.
  9. API9:2023 - Improper Inventory Management - APIs expose more endpoints than documented.
  10. API10:2023 - Unsafe Consumption of APIs - Trusting data from third-party APIs without validation.

Resources

Download the full document, methodology, and data files from our GitHub repository.

REST Security Cheat Sheet

Introduction

REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for building web services. This cheat sheet covers security best practices for REST APIs.

HTTPS

Always use HTTPS. Do not redirect HTTP to HTTPS - reject HTTP connections entirely in production.

Access Control

  • Use standard authentication mechanisms (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect)
  • Never expose credentials in URLs
  • Implement proper session timeout
  • Use secure, random tokens

Input Validation

  • Validate content-type header
  • Validate and sanitize all input
  • Use parameterized queries

Configuration Security

  • Disable debug endpoints and verbose error messages in production
  • Remove unnecessary HTTP methods (TRACE, OPTIONS if not needed)
  • Configure strict CORS policies - never use wildcard (*) for credentials
  • Set appropriate security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options)
  • Disable server version disclosure
  • Use environment isolation - separate dev/staging/production configurations
  • Apply principle of least privilege to service accounts
  • Regular security audits of configuration files

Rate Limiting

Implement rate limiting to prevent abuse. Use 429 Too Many Requests response code.

Error Handling

Return generic error messages. Log detailed errors server-side only.

Claude can be configured for agentic behavior using project-specific configuration files.

For persistent project context, Claude supports a CLAUDE.md file placed in the workspace root. This file allows you to define:

Seccomp security profiles for Docker

Secure computing mode (seccomp) is a Linux kernel feature used to restrict the system calls available to running containers.

Default behavior

By default, Docker uses a seccomp profile that disables 44 system calls out of the 300+ available, providing moderate security while maintaining general utility.

Blocked system calls include:

  • mount, umount2 - Prevent container filesystem tampering
  • chroot - Prevent escape via chroot
  • ptrace - Prevent process debugging/injection
  • reboot, kexec_load - Prevent system reboots
  • open_by_handle_at - Prevent file descriptor attacks
  • init_module, delete_module - Prevent kernel module loading

The full profile is available in the Moby source code at https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/profiles/seccomp/default.json

Pass a profile for a container

To use a custom profile, pass --security-opt seccomp=/path/to/profile.json to the docker run command...

## Comparison: browser sandboxing, process isolation, and same-origin policy

- **Chromium:** Chromium's security architecture describes the browser as a multi-process application and uses sandboxing to restrict renderer privileges. This boundary is aimed at containing damage if web content triggers a renderer compromise; it does not replace web-platform rules about which origins may access which resources.
- **Firefox:** Mozilla's documentation describes Firefox as using separate content processes together with sandbox restrictions to reduce the capabilities available to web content code. Like Chromium's model, this is a containment boundary around browser processes rather than a rule that defines normal cross-site data access in page scripts.
- **Same-origin policy:** MDN defines the same-origin policy as a core browser security mechanism that restricts how a document or script from one origin can interact with resources from another origin. This boundary governs web content interactions at the platform level, but it is not the same as an operating-system sandbox and does not by itself contain arbitrary native process compromise.

turns.tool_response:
Docker security

There are four major areas to consider when reviewing Docker security:

  • The intrinsic security of the kernel and its support for namespaces and cgroups
  • The attack surface of the Docker daemon itself
  • Loopholes in the container configuration profile, either by default, or when customized by users
  • The "hardening" security features of the kernel and how they interact with containers

Kernel namespaces

Docker containers are very similar to LXC containers, and they have similar security features. When you start a container with docker run, behind the scenes Docker creates a set of namespaces and control groups for the container.

Control groups

Control Groups are another key component of Linux containers. They implement resource accounting and limiting. They provide many useful metrics, but they also help ensure that each container gets its fair share of memory, CPU, disk I/O.

Docker daemon attack surface

Running containers with Docker implies running the Docker daemon. The Docker daemon requires root privileges. You should be aware of some important details:

  • Only trusted users should be allowed to control your Docker daemon
  • If you bind the daemon to a TCP socket, secure it with TLS

Linux kernel capabilities

By default, Docker starts containers with a restricted set of capabilities. Capabilities turn the binary "root/non-root" dichotomy into a fine-grained access control system.

Seccomp security profiles

Docker uses seccomp to limit the syscalls available to containers. The default seccomp profile blocks around 44 syscalls out of over 300.

Introduction

import json
import csv
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Dict, Any

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class DataProcessor:
    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
        self.config = config
        self.batch_size = config.get('processing', {}).get('batch_size', 100)
        self.format = config.get('processing', {}).get('output_format', 'json')
        self.processed_count = 0
    
    def process_directory(self, input_dir: str, output_dir: str) -> List[str]:
        input_path = Path(input_dir)
        output_path = Path(output_dir)
        output_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        results = []
        for file_path in input_path.glob('*.csv'):
            logger.info(f'Processing {file_path.name}')
            output_file = output_path / f'{file_path.stem}.{self.format}'
            self.process_file(file_path, output_file)
            results.append(str(output_file))
        
        return results
    
    def process_file(self, input_file: Path, output_file: Path) -> None:
        with open(input_file, 'r') as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            records = list(reader)
        
        transformed = [self.transform_record(r) for r in records]
        self.processed_count += len(transformed)
        
        with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(transformed, f, indent=2)
    
    def transform_record(self, record: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            'id': record.get('id', ''),
            'name': record.get('name', '').strip().title(),
            'value': float(record.get('value', 0)),
            'processed': True
        }

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Iterable


def chunked(items: list[dict], size: int) -> list[list[dict]]:
    if size <= 0:
        raise ValueError('size must be positive')
    return [items[i:i + size] for i in range(0, len(items), size)]


def summarize_jobs(jobs: Iterable[dict]) -> dict:
    jobs = list(jobs)
    total = len(jobs)
    enabled = sum(1 for job in jobs if job.get('enabled'))
    return {
        'total': total,
        'enabled': enabled,
        'disabled': total - enabled,
        'generated_at': datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z',
    }
EOF

import argparse
import logging
import subprocess

from config import get_log_level, get_server_port, load_config
from utils import summarize_jobs


logger = logging.getLogger('jobrunner')


def configure_logging(level: str) -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=getattr(logging, level.upper(), logging.INFO),
        format='%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s'
    )


def restart_worker(service_name: str) -> int:
    logger.warning('Restarting worker service %s', service_name)
    result = subprocess.run(
        ['pkill', '-f', service_name],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode not in (0, 1):
        logger.error('pkill failed: %s', result.stderr.strip())
    return result.returncode


def build_status(config: dict) -> dict:
    jobs = config.get('jobs', {}).get('definitions', [])
    return {
        'port': get_server_port(config),
        'summary': summarize_jobs(jobs),
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Job runner control utility')
    parser.add_argument('--config', default=None, help='Path to config file')
    parser.add_argument('--status', action='store_true', help='Print status summary')
    parser.add_argument('--restart-worker', metavar='NAME', help='Restart a worker process by name')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    config = load_config(args.config)
    configure_logging(get_log_level(config))

    if args.status:
        status = build_status(config)
        print(f"Server port: {status['port']}")
        print(f"Jobs total: {status['summary']['total']}")
        print(f"Jobs enabled: {status['summary']['enabled']}")

    if args.restart_worker:
        return restart_worker(args.restart_worker)

    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

def build_summary(records: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    normalized = []
    for row in records:
        record = Record(
            user_id=row['user_id'],
            name=row['name'],
            active=row.get('active', False),
            score=row.get('score', 0),
            tags=normalize_tags(row.get('tags', [])),

        normalized.append(record)

    high_value = [r.name for r in normalized if r.is_high_value()]

        'active': len([r for r in normalized if r.active]),
        'average_score': average_score(records),
        'high_value_users': high_value,
    }


def load_hook(script_path: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not script_path:
        return None
    path = Path(script_path)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'hook script not found: {script_path}')
    return path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')

class ApplicationServer:
    def __init__(self, config_path: str):

        self.worker_pool: Optional[WorkerPool] = None
        self.running = False
        self._setup_signal_handlers()
    
    def _setup_signal_handlers(self):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, self._handle_shutdown)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, self._handle_shutdown)
    
    def _handle_shutdown(self, signum, frame):
        logger.info(f"Received signal {signum}, initiating graceful shutdown")
        self.running = False
        if self.worker_pool:

        self.running = True
        num_workers = self.config.get('workers', 4)
        self.worker_pool = WorkerPool(num_workers)
        self.worker_pool.start()

            try:

            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Error processing queue: {e}")
        
        logger.info("Server shutdown complete")


def main():

    server = ApplicationServer(config_path)

#!/bin/bash
# Process management script

PID_FILE="/tmp/project/logs/app.pid"
LOG_FILE="/tmp/project/logs/app.log"

start() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        PID=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if ps -p $PID > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "Application already running with PID $PID"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    echo "Starting application..."
    cd /tmp/project
    python src/main.py >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$PID_FILE"
    echo "Started with PID $(cat $PID_FILE)"
}

stop() {
    if [ ! -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        echo "PID file not found"
        exit 1
    fi
    PID=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
    echo "Stopping application (PID: $PID)..."
    kill -SIGTERM $PID 2>/dev/null
    sleep 5
    if ps -p $PID > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Process still running, sending SIGKILL..."
        kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null
    fi
    rm -f "$PID_FILE"
    echo "Stopped"
}

status() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        PID=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if ps -p $PID > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "Running (PID: $PID)"
        else
            echo "Not running (stale PID file)"
        fi
    else
        echo "Not running"
    fi
}

case "$1" in
    start) start ;;
    stop) stop ;;
    restart) stop; sleep 2; start ;;
    status) status ;;
    *) echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|restart|status}" ;;
esac

def process_customer_csv(input_path, output_path):
    """Process customer CSV and convert to standard format."""
    results = []
    errors = []
    
    with open(input_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row_num, row in enumerate(reader, 1):
            try:
                record = CustomerRecord(
                    id=row['customer_id'],
                    name=row['name'],
                    email=row['email'],
                    phone=validate_phone(row.get('phone', '')),
                    country=row.get('country', 'US')
                )
                results.append(record)
            except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
                logger.error(f"Encoding error on row {row_num}: {e}")
                errors.append({'row': row_num, 'error': str(e)})
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Validation error on row {row_num}: {e}")

    with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        if results:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=results[0].to_dict().keys())
            writer.writeheader()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess
import sys
import os
import tempfile

def detect_encoding(file_path):
    """Use system file command to detect encoding."""
    result = subprocess.run(['file', '-b', '--mime-encoding', file_path], 
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    return result.stdout.strip()

def convert_file(input_path, output_path):
    """Convert file to UTF-8, handling mixed encodings."""
    encoding = detect_encoding(input_path)
    print(f"Detected encoding: {encoding}")
    
    if encoding == 'utf-8':
        # Copy as-is but remove null bytes
        with open(input_path, 'rb') as f:
            content = f.read()
        content = content.replace(b'\x00', b'')
        with open(output_path, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(content)
    else:
        # Convert using iconv
        temp_path = tempfile.mktemp()
        cmd = f"iconv -f {encoding} -t utf-8//IGNORE '{input_path}' > '{temp_path}' 2>/dev/null || cp '{input_path}' '{temp_path}'"
        os.system(cmd)
        
        # Remove null bytes and move to destination
        with open(temp_path, 'rb') as f:
            content = f.read()
        content = content.replace(b'\x00', b'')
        with open(output_path, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(content)
        os.remove(temp_path)
    
    print(f"Converted: {output_path}")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: fix_encoding.py <input> <output>")
        sys.exit(1)
    convert_file(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

cat > /tmp/analysis/scripts/etl.py << 'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import json

BASE = Path('/tmp/analysis')
RAW_SALES = BASE / 'data/raw/sales.csv'
RAW_USERS = BASE / 'data/raw/users.json'
CLEAN_SALES = BASE / 'data/processed/clean_sales.csv'


def load_sales(path=RAW_SALES):
    df = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=['order_date'])
    return df


def load_users(path=RAW_USERS):
    with open(path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return pd.DataFrame(data)


def clean_sales(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    df['returned'] = df['returned'].astype(str).str.lower().map({'true': True, 'false': False})
    df = df[df['returned'] == False]
    df['discount_pct'] = df['discount_pct'].fillna(0)
    df['net_revenue'] = (df['units'] * df['unit_price'] * (1 - df['discount_pct'])).round(2)
    return df


def save_clean_sales(df: pd.DataFrame, path=CLEAN_SALES):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df.to_csv(path, index=False)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sales = load_sales()
    clean = clean_sales(sales)
    save_clean_sales(clean)
    print(f'Saved {len(clean)} clean rows to {CLEAN_SALES}')
EOF

cat > /tmp/analysis/scripts/analysis.py << 'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import json

BASE = Path('/tmp/analysis')
CLEAN_SALES = BASE / 'data/processed/clean_sales.csv'
USERS = BASE / 'data/raw/users.json'
REPORT = BASE / 'reports/monthly_summary.md'


def load_users():
    with open(USERS) as f:
        return pd.DataFrame(json.load(f))


def build_summary():
    sales = pd.read_csv(CLEAN_SALES, parse_dates=['order_date'])
    users = load_users()
    merged = sales.merge(users[['customer_id', 'segment', 'active']], on='customer_id', how='left')
    merged['month'] = merged['order_date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)

    monthly = merged.groupby('month').agg(
        orders=('order_id', 'count'),
        revenue=('net_revenue', 'sum'),
        avg_order_value=('net_revenue', 'mean')
    ).reset_index()

    segment = merged.groupby('segment').agg(
        customers=('customer_id', 'nunique'),
        revenue=('net_revenue', 'sum')
    ).reset_index().sort_values('revenue', ascending=False)

    top_products = merged.groupby('product').agg(
        revenue=('net_revenue', 'sum'),
        units=('units', 'sum')
    ).reset_index().sort_values('revenue', ascending=False)

    return monthly, segment, top_products


def write_report():
    monthly, segment, top_products = build_summary()
    lines = []
    lines.append('# Monthly Sales Summary')
    lines.append('')
    lines.append('## Monthly performance')
    lines.append(monthly.to_markdown(index=False))
    lines.append('')
    lines.append('## Revenue by customer segment')
    lines.append(segment.to_markdown(index=False))
    lines.append('')
    lines.append('## Top products')
    lines.append(top_products.head(5).to_markdown(index=False))
    REPORT.write_text('\n'.join(lines))
    print(f'Wrote report to {REPORT}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    write_report()
EOF

from pathlib import Path
import json

        users = pd.DataFrame(json.load(f))

def transform(sales, users):
    sales = sales.copy()

    clean = transform(sales, users)
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

import pandas as pd
import json
from pathlib import Path
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def load_sales_data(filepath):
    """Load and validate sales CSV data."""
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df)} sales records")
    return df

def load_customer_data(filepath):
    """Load customer JSON data."""
    with open(filepath) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)
    logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df)} customer records")
    return df

def calculate_totals(df):
    """Add total_amount column."""
    df['total_amount'] = df['quantity'] * df['unit_price']
    return df

def merge_customer_info(sales_df, customer_df):
    """Merge sales with customer details."""
    merged = sales_df.merge(customer_df[['customer_id', 'type', 'name']], 
                            on='customer_id', how='left')
    return merged

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sales = load_sales_data('data/raw/sales.csv')
    sales = calculate_totals(sales)
    sales.to_csv('data/processed/clean_sales.csv', index=False)
    logger.info("ETL complete")
EOF

import pandas as pd
import sys

def validate_sales(filepath):
    """Run data quality checks on sales data."""
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    issues = []
    
    # Check for nulls in critical columns
    null_counts = df[['transaction_id', 'date', 'quantity', 'unit_price']].isnull().sum()
    if null_counts.any():
        issues.append(f"Null values found: {null_counts.to_dict()}")
    
    # Check for negative quantities
    if (df['quantity'] < 0).any():
        issues.append("Negative quantities detected")
    
    # Check for duplicate transaction IDs
    dupes = df['transaction_id'].duplicated().sum()
    if dupes > 0:
        issues.append(f"{dupes} duplicate transaction IDs")
    
    if issues:
        print("Validation FAILED:")
        for issue in issues:
            print(f"  - {issue}")
        return False
    else:
        print("Validation PASSED")
        return True

if __name__ == '__main__':
    filepath = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'data/raw/sales.csv'
    validate_sales(filepath)

import pandas as pd
import json
from pathlib import Path
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

RAW_DIR = Path('/tmp/analysis/data/raw')
PROCESSED_DIR = Path('/tmp/analysis/data/processed')

def load_sales_data():
    """Load and validate sales CSV data."""
    sales_path = RAW_DIR / 'sales.csv'
    df = pd.read_csv(sales_path)
    logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df)} sales records")
    return df

def load_customer_data():
    """Load customer data from JSON."""
    users_path = RAW_DIR / 'users.json'
    with open(users_path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return pd.DataFrame(data['customers'])

def clean_sales_data(df):
    """Apply cleaning transformations."""
    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    df['total_amount'] = df['quantity'] * df['unit_price']
    df = df.dropna(subset=['transaction_id', 'product_id'])
    return df

def merge_with_customers(sales_df, customers_df):
    """Join sales with customer tier information."""
    merged = sales_df.merge(
        customers_df[['customer_id', 'tier', 'signup_date']],
        on='customer_id',
        how='left'
    )
    return merged

def save_processed_data(df, filename):
    """Save processed data to CSV."""
    output_path = PROCESSED_DIR / filename
    df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    logger.info(f"Saved processed data to {output_path}")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sales = load_sales_data()
    sales = clean_sales_data(sales)
    save_processed_data(sales, 'clean_sales.csv')

import pandas as pd
import json
from pathlib import Path
import logging
from datetime import datetime
import time
import sys

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.FileHandler('/tmp/analysis/logs/etl.log'),
        logging.StreamHandler()
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def extract_sales():
    logger.info("Extracting sales data")
    df = pd.read_csv('/tmp/analysis/data/raw/sales.csv')
    logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df)} sales records")
    return df

def extract_users():
    logger.info("Extracting user data")
    with open('/tmp/analysis/data/raw/users.json') as f:
        users = json.load(f)
    df = pd.DataFrame(users)
    logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df)} user records")
    return df

def transform_data(sales_df, users_df):
    logger.info("Transforming data")
    sales_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(sales_df['date'])
    sales_df['revenue'] = sales_df['amount'] * sales_df['quantity']
    sales_df['month'] = sales_df['date'].dt.to_period('M')
    
    # Merge with user data
    merged = sales_df.merge(users_df[['user_id', 'plan']], 
                           left_on='customer_id', right_on='user_id', how='left')
    return merged

def load_to_processed(df):
    output_path = '/tmp/analysis/data/processed/clean_sales.csv'
    df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    logger.info(f"Saved processed data to {output_path}")

def main():
    logger.info("=== Starting ETL Pipeline v1.2.0 ===")
    try:
        sales_df = extract_sales()
        users_df = extract_users()
        transformed = transform_data(sales_df, users_df)
        load_to_processed(transformed)
        logger.info("=== ETL Completed Successfully ===")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"ETL Failed: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    df['total'] = df['quantity'] * df['unit_price']
    df = df.dropna(subset=['product_id', 'customer_id'])
    df = df[df['quantity'] > 0]
    df = df[df['unit_price'] > 0]
    removed = initial_count - len(df)
    logger.info(f'Removed {removed} invalid records, {len(df)} remaining')
    return df

def enrich_with_user_data(sales_df, users_list):
    users_df = pd.DataFrame(users_list)
    merged = sales_df.merge(users_df[['user_id', 'tier', 'contract_value']], 
                           left_on='customer_id', right_on='user_id', how='left')
    return merged

def save_processed(df, output_path='/tmp/analysis/data/processed/clean_sales.csv'):
    df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    logger.info(f'Saved {len(df)} records to {output_path}')

def validate_output(filepath):
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    assert len(df) >= 1000, f'Insufficient records: {len(df)}'
    max_date = pd.to_datetime(df['date']).max()
    assert max_date >= pd.Timestamp('2024-12-31'), f'Data incomplete, max date: {max_date}'
    logger.info('Validation passed')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        logger.info('Starting ETL pipeline v2.1.0')
        sales_raw, users_raw = load_raw_data()
        sales_clean = clean_sales_data(sales_raw)
        sales_enriched = enrich_with_user_data(sales_clean, users_raw)
        save_processed(sales_enriched)
        validate_output('/tmp/analysis/data/processed/clean_sales.csv')
        logger.info('ETL completed successfully')
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f'ETL failed: {e}')
        sys.exit(1)
EOF

from pathlib import Path
import json
import pandas as pd

BASE = Path('/tmp/analysis')
RAW_SALES = BASE / 'data/raw/sales.csv'
RAW_USERS = BASE / 'data/raw/users.json'
OUT = BASE / 'data/processed/clean_sales.csv'


def load_inputs():
    sales = pd.read_csv(RAW_SALES, parse_dates=['order_date'])
    users = pd.read_json(RAW_USERS)
    return sales, users


def clean_sales(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    df = df[df['units'] > 0]
    df['discount_pct'] = df['discount_pct'].fillna(0).clip(lower=0, upper=0.5)
    df['month'] = df['order_date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)
    df['revenue'] = (df['units'] * df['unit_price'] * (1 - df['discount_pct'])).round(2)
    return df


def enrich_sales(sales: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return sales.merge(users, on='customer_id', how='left')


def run():
    sales, users = load_inputs()
    clean = clean_sales(sales)
    enriched = enrich_sales(clean, users)
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    enriched.to_csv(OUT, index=False)
    print(f'wrote {len(enriched)} rows to {OUT}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run()
EOF

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

BASE = Path('/tmp/analysis')
FILE = BASE / 'data/processed/clean_sales.csv'
REPORT = BASE / 'reports/monthly_summary.md'


def monthly_summary(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    grouped = df.groupby('month').agg(
        orders=('order_id', 'count'),
        units=('units', 'sum'),
        revenue=('revenue', 'sum'),
        avg_order_value=('revenue', 'mean')
    ).reset_index()
    return grouped.sort_values('month')


def segment_summary(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if 'segment' not in df.columns:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    return df.groupby('segment').agg(
        revenue=('revenue', 'sum'),
        customers=('customer_id', 'nunique')
    ).reset_index().sort_values('revenue', ascending=False)


def write_report(monthly: pd.DataFrame, segment: pd.DataFrame):
    lines = ['# Monthly Sales Summary', '']
    lines.append('## Revenue by Month')
    lines.append('')
    lines.append(monthly.to_markdown(index=False))
    if not segment.empty:
        lines.append('')
        lines.append('## Revenue by Segment')
        lines.append('')
        lines.append(segment.to_markdown(index=False))
    REPORT.write_text('\n'.join(lines))
    print(f'wrote report to {REPORT}')


def run():
    df = pd.read_csv(FILE)
    monthly = monthly_summary(df)
    segment = segment_summary(df)
    write_report(monthly, segment)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ETL pipeline for sales data processing."""

import pandas as pd
import json
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

DATA_DIR = Path('/tmp/analysis/data')

def load_raw_sales():
    """Load raw sales CSV with validation."""
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / 'raw' / 'sales.csv')
    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    return df

def load_customers():
    """Load customer data from JSON."""
    with open(DATA_DIR / 'raw' / 'users.json') as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return pd.DataFrame(data['customers'])

def clean_sales_data(df):
    """Apply cleaning transformations."""
    # Remove duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['transaction_id'])
    # Validate amounts
    df = df[df['total_amount'] > 0]
    # Standardize region names
    df['region'] = df['region'].str.strip().str.title()
    return df

def enrich_with_customer_data(sales_df, customers_df):
    """Join sales with customer info."""

import pandas as pd
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_style("whitegrid")

def load_data():
    sales = pd.read_csv('/tmp/analysis/data/raw/sales.csv')
    with open('/tmp/analysis/data/raw/users.json') as f:
        users = pd.DataFrame(json.load(f)['users'])
    return sales, users

def generate_monthly_summary(output_dir='/tmp/analysis/reports'):
    sales, users = load_data()
    
    sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(sales['date'])
    sales['revenue'] = sales['amount']
    
    summary = sales.groupby('product_category').agg({
        'revenue': ['sum', 'mean', 'count'],
        'transaction_id': 'count'
    }).round(2)
    
    summary.columns = ['total_revenue', 'avg_transaction', 'transaction_count', 'txns']
    summary = summary.drop('txns', axis=1)
    
    merged = sales.merge(users, left_on='customer_id', right_on='id', how='left')
    segment_revenue = merged.groupby('segment')['amount'].sum().round(2)
    
    output_path = Path(output_dir) / 'monthly_summary.md'
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write("# Sales Analysis Report - January 2024\n\n")
        f.write("## Summary by Product Category\n\n")
        f.write(summary.to_markdown())
        f.write("\n\n## Revenue by Customer Segment\n\n")
        f.write(segment_revenue.to_frame().to_markdown())
    
    print(f"Report generated: {output_path}")
    return summary, segment_revenue

def plot_revenue_by_region(output_dir='/tmp/analysis/reports/figures'):
    sales, _ = load_data()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    sales.groupby('region')['amount'].sum().plot(kind='bar', ax=ax, color='steelblue')
    ax.set_title('Revenue by Region - January 2024')
    ax.set_ylabel('Revenue ($)')
    plt.tight_layout()
    output_path = Path(output_dir) / 'revenue_by_region.png'
    plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=150)
    print(f"Chart saved: {output_path}")
    return output_path

if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == 'plot':
        plot_revenue_by_region()
    else:
        generate_monthly_summary()
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# Process manager for inventory application
# Handles graceful shutdowns and restarts

PIDFILE="/var/run/inventory.pid"
LOCKFILE="/var/lock/inventory.lock"

log_message() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1" | tee -a /var/log/inventory/manager.log
}

graceful_shutdown() {
    log_message "Received SIGTERM, initiating graceful shutdown..."
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
        PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
        log_message "Sending SIGTERM to process $PID"
        kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null
        
        # Wait up to 30 seconds for process to terminate gracefully
        for i in {1..30}; do
            if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
                log_message "Process $PID terminated gracefully after ${i}s"
                rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$LOCKFILE"
                return 0
            fi
            log_message "Waiting for process to terminate... (${i}/30)"
            sleep 1
        done
        
        # Force kill if still running after 30 seconds
        log_message "WARNING: Process did not terminate gracefully, sending SIGKILL..."
        kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null
        rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$LOCKFILE"
    else
        log_message "No PID file found, process may not be running"
    fi
}

force_restart() {
    log_message "Force restart requested"
    graceful_shutdown
    sleep 2
    log_message "Starting new process instance..."
    /opt/inventory/bin/startup.sh
}

status_check() {
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
        PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
        if kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_message "Process $PID is running"
            return 0
        else
            log_message "Stale PID file found, process is not running"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        log_message "No PID file found"
        return 1
    fi
}

trap graceful_shutdown SIGTERM SIGINT

case "$1" in
    stop|shutdown)
        graceful_shutdown
        ;;
    restart)
        force_restart
        ;;
    status)
        status_check
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 {stop|restart|status}"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
EOF

    log_message "Force restart requested"
    graceful_shutdown
    sleep 2
    log_message "Starting new process instance..."
    /opt/inventory/bin/startup.sh
}

status_check() {
    if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
        PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
        if kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_message "Process $PID is running"
            return 0
        else
            log_message "Stale PID file found, process is not running"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        log_message "No PID file found"
        return 1
    fi
}

trap graceful_shutdown SIGTERM SIGINT

case "$1" in
    stop|shutdown)
        graceful_shutdown
        ;;
    restart)
        force_restart
        ;;
    status)
        status_check
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 {stop|restart|status}"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

import csv
from datetime import datetime

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ['id', 'timestamp', 'value', 'category']

def parse_csv_data(filepath):
    records = []
    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            row['parsed_at'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
            records.append(row)
    return records

def validate_schema(record):
    for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
        if field not in record or not record[field]:
            return False
    try:
        float(record['value'])
        return True
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return False

def clean_old_files(directory, pattern='*.tmp', max_age_days=7):
    """Remove temporary files older than max_age_days"""
    from pathlib import Path
    import os
    import time
    
    threshold = time.time() - (max_age_days * 86400)
    removed = []
    for f in Path(directory).glob(pattern):
        if f.stat().st_mtime < threshold:
            f.unlink()
            removed.append(str(f))
    return removed
EOF

import os
import signal
import sys
import time
import logging
from datetime import datetime

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class WorkerProcess:
    def __init__(self, worker_id, config):
        self.worker_id = worker_id
        self.config = config
        self.running = True
        self.pid = os.getpid()
        
    def handle_shutdown(self, signum, frame):
        logger.info(f'Worker {self.worker_id} received shutdown signal')
        self.running = False
        
    def process_job(self, job):
        """Process a single job from the queue"""
        start = time.time()
        # Simulate processing
        time.sleep(0.1)
        duration = time.time() - start
        logger.info(f'Worker {self.worker_id} processed job {job["id"]} in {duration:.2f}s')
        return {'status': 'completed', 'duration': duration}
        
    def run(self):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, self.handle_shutdown)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, self.handle_shutdown)
        logger.info(f'Worker {self.worker_id} started with PID {self.pid}')
        
        while self.running:
            # Poll for jobs
            time.sleep(1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    worker_id = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '1'
    worker = WorkerProcess(worker_id, {})
    worker.run()

    rows = []

        for row in reader:

            rows.append(row)

    total = sum(r['amount'] for r in rows)
    pending = [r for r in rows if r['status'] == 'pending']
    complete = [r for r in rows if r['status'] == 'complete']
    return {
        'count': len(rows),
        'total_amount': round(total, 2),
        'pending_count': len(pending),
        'complete_count': len(complete),
    }


def export_summary(summary, output_path):

        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)

import logging
import psycopg2
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def setup_logging(level, log_file):
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=getattr(logging, level),
        format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
        handlers=[
            logging.FileHandler(log_file),
            logging.StreamHandler()
        ]
    )

def get_db_connection(url):
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    conn = psycopg2.connect(
        host=parsed.hostname,
        port=parsed.port or 5432,
        database=parsed.path[1:],
        user=parsed.username,
        password=parsed.password
    )
    return conn
EOF

The asyncio library provides infrastructure for writing single-threaded concurrent code using coroutines, multiplexing I/O access over sockets and other resources...

High-level APIs

TaskGroup

New in version 3.11.

An asynchronous context manager that makes it easier to wait for a group of related tasks. When entered, it returns a new task group. Tasks can be added to the group using create_task(). When the context manager exits, it waits for all tasks to finish.

async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
    task1 = tg.create_task(some_coroutine())
    task2 = tg.create_task(another_coroutine())
print("Both tasks have completed now.")

Exception handling

If any tasks in a TaskGroup fail with an exception other than asyncio.CancelledError, those exceptions are combined into an ExceptionGroup or BaseExceptionGroup...
